newsitem.title: USA: Minn. lawmaker wants slot machines at racetrack.
newsitem.headline: Minn. lawmaker wants slot machines at racetrack.

text.p: A Minnesota legislator opposed to the current proposal for a new Twins baseball stadium said Friday that he wants to place video slot machines at a horse racing track to generate revenue to tie the team to its current home.

Rep. Todd Van Dellen, R-Plymouth, said the metropolitan sports facilities commission could use revenue from slot machines at the Canterbury Downs racetrack to buy enough tickets to tie the team to the Metrodome.

The Twins current lease runs through 2011, but gives the team an escape window in 1998 if ticket sales fall below 80 percent of the American League average or if it loses money each of the three years 1995, 1996 and 1997, Van Dellen noted.
The current proposal to build a $300 million stadium is "too expensive" given that $20 million could tie them to the Metrodome for the next 14 years, Van Dellen said.
Van Dellen said he would add his proposal as an amendment to existing proposals.

A state House committee voted on Wednesday not to advance a bill to help finance the stadium. The bill's sponsors had not yet decided how to respond to the House Local Government and Metropolitan Affairs Committee vote.
A Senate committee earlier eliminated public funding for the stadium before approving it. The stadium is expected to cost $250 million to $300 million or more if a retractable roof is added.
